ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Elbow dislocation: 5

After reduction of a stable elbow dislocation, follow-up emphasizes appropriately timed motion rather than unnecessarily prolonged immobilization. Which common post-injury complication is this rehabilitation strategy intended to reduce once stability has been confirmed?

  1. Complex elbow dislocation
  2. Terrible triad injury
  3. Brachial artery injury
  4. Post-injury elbow stiffness
  5. Simple elbow dislocation
Answer and explanation

Post-injury elbow stiffness

Prolonged immobilization can contribute to restricted elbow motion, so rehabilitation depends on confirmed stability.

Option explanations

Post-injury elbow stiffness: Prolonged immobilization can contribute to restricted elbow motion, so rehabilitation depends on confirmed stability.

Simple elbow dislocation: A dislocation without a major associated fracture is termed simple, but ligament injury and instability can still occur. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Complex elbow dislocation: An elbow dislocation with an associated fracture is complex. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Terrible triad injury: Elbow dislocation with radial head and coronoid fractures is the terrible triad. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Brachial artery injury: Elbow dislocation can threaten the brachial artery and distal perfusion. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
